title: Solar power and batteries
purpose: Teach why polar solar panels stand tall, how a battery stores and spills power, and what darkness does to a base.

beats.label: model

beats.blanket_l: Panel raised {blanket} m above the ground

beats.label: diagram
beats.empty: Empty: lights and heaters go dark

captions: Near the pole the Sun stays low, so solar panels stand tall and upright.
This NASA design hangs a {kw} kW panel from a {mast} m mast.
It turns to keep facing the Sun.
A battery works like a water tank: sunlight fills it, the base drains it.
When the tank is full, any extra power spills away and is lost.
So spare power is best used while you have it.
When the Sun hides, nothing flows in. The base lives on the tank.
If the tank runs dry, the lights and heaters go dark.
ends_on: Use spare power before it spills, and keep enough in the tank for the dark.
